matchingNotes: Coordinates copied exactly from published GTFS, never invented or interpolated.
App route 10 matches are selected using direction_id=1 source stop_times observation counts, 3335 historical trips.
Non10 matches only identify the same named physical stop from route10 direction1. They do not verify routes 501, 40 or 53 serving that point or establish their stop side.
Exact literal Cyrillic-name matches: 0; accepted matches use explicit transliteration/translation mappings.

Route10 stop 16 has two source stop IDs with the same name and many observations. Primary candidate is the first encountered stop in the source ordered sequence; app has only one instance. This is a source-name ambiguity, not fabricated data.

source.name: Astana historical GTFS — Mansurova et al. (2025)
source.selectionMethod: For this route_short_name and direction_id=1, sort each observed trip by numeric stop_sequence and count exact ordered stop_id tuples. Select the most frequent tuple. The entire selected observed pattern is retained; no missing stop is inferred and no stop is deleted.
source.limitations: Historical observed trip pattern, not a verified current or official complete route. Coordinates and stop IDs are source GTFS; original Latin/transliterated stop names retained. No live transit, timetable, passenger count or bus capacity is supplied by this integration.
source.metadataCaution: Source route_long_name duplicates route 10 (Astana Railway Station – International Airport – Astana Railway Station). That field is not used to identify endpoints. Identity comes from route_short_name=12 and trips.route_id; endpoints come from the selected stop_times pattern.

simulation.capacityAssumptionNote: 100 passengers is a demonstration-model assumption, not measured or operator-sourced capacity. Existing occupancy predictions must be presented as simulated estimates, not live data.
